currentContext.business: IndiQube began as a managed workspace provider and has evolved into an integrated managed spaces platform operating at the intersection of real estate, interiors, operations, technology and sustainability. It delivers plug-and-play managed workspaces (Grow), customised interior design & build/retrofit (DesignQube), managed/facility services for workspaces and retail (IndiQare), green transformation solutions including solar and renovation (Eco), and a connecting digital technology layer (MiQube/ServiQube). risks.note: Global Capability Centres alone contribute 56% of revenue and 49% of occupied area, making the company's growth meaningfully dependent on continued GCC leasing demand and site-selection decisions.

Bengaluru is described as the company's core anchor market and carries by far the largest share of the network (70 of 130 centres, 138K of 215K seats, 6.20 million of 9.66 million sq. ft. AUM), exposing performance to that single city's office-market cycle.

Management flags renewed pressure from the Middle East conflict, rising commodity prices, tighter financial conditions, elevated public debt and continued trade tensions as downside risks to the operating environment in which the company's enterprise/GCC clients make expansion decisions.

risks.risk: Domestic energy-price volatility and fiscal support risk
risks.note: The MD&A Outlook explicitly flags energy volatility and moderating fiscal support as persistent (if manageable) risks to India's growth trajectory, on which the company's demand depends.

risks.risk: Asset-liability mismatch inherent in the managed-workspace model
risks.note: The business depends on aligning shorter client lock-ins (34 months) against longer landlord lock-in (38 months) and interior fit-out capex payback (36 months); any weakening of client retention or occupancy ramp-up relative to these commitments would strain the asset-light model's economics.

one-line thesis: Indiqube delivered record FY26 results (37% revenue growth, 21% EBITDA margin) driven by aggressive GCC-led absorption and operational leverage, while differentiating via captive solar assets that structurally lower costs and attract power-guzzling data/GCC clients. Guidance remains robust at 25-30% top-line growth with sustained margin expansion despite slight capex intensity due to solar and material inflation.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,469 Cr (+37% YoY); EBITDA: >INR 300 Cr (+60% YoY), Margin 21% (vs 18% FY25); PAT: INR 125 Cr (+145% YoY), Margin 9% (vs 5% FY25); Order Book: Implicit via 1.6 Mn sq ft addition & 9.66 Mn sq ft AUM (18-24 mo conversion); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but Lease Liabilities tracking revenue growth; One-offs: Solar depreciation (accelerated 40%) boosting future PAT, Capex overshoot (INR 413 Cr vs INR 360 Cr guided) due to INR 73 Cr solar investment.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 25-30%; EBITDA Margin: 18-21%; Order Inflow: 1.5-2.0 Mn sq ft annual addition (33k-44k seats); Capex: ~INR 1,650/sq ft for interiors + INR 125-150 Cr for 30-35 MW solar addition.
order book & pipeline: Area Under Management (AUM) at 9.66 Mn sq ft; Rent-paying area 7.84 Mn sq ft; Occupied area 6.23 Mn sq ft (81% occupancy); 15 new centers launched in FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: Core Workspace (85% revenue, 18-21% margin); VAS (15% revenue, up from 12%, targeting 17-18%; includes IT products, design-build, transport); Solar (INR 22-23 Cr annual savings, 26.7 MW operational/soon-operational).
growth verticals / optionality: Tier-2 city expansion (e.g., Coimbatore) as a 10-year story; Hub-and-Spoke model capturing 20-25% of large MNC portfolios as 'spokes'; Micro-data centers within facilities for power-guzzling GCCs; Renovation of Grade-B to Grade-A assets (25% of portfolio).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps to 21% driven by operating leverage and mature center stabilization (85-90% occupancy); VAS margins lower (10-15%) but accretive to scale/stickiness; Cost headwind: Material inflation added INR 1/sq ft to capex (5-7% bump); Solar savings offset rising grid power costs.
capex / expansion: Total FY26 Capex INR 413 Cr (Interiors: INR 248-256 Cr; Design-Build: INR 50 Cr; Solar: INR 73 Cr; Vendor advances: ~INR 30 Cr); FY27 Solar Capex guidance INR 125-150 Cr for 30-35 MW; Per sq ft capex trended to INR 1,650.
capital allocation: Focus on organic growth (1.5-2 Mn sq ft/year); Strategic solar investments for cost arbitrage and client acquisition; No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not discussed in transcript.
risks & watch-items: Quarterly occupancy volatility (ended Q4 at 81% vs 85% prior); Material cost inflation (war impact); Tier-2 supply maturity challenges; Concentration in South India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra); Potential AI impact on low-end hiring (mitigated by premiumization).
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, and strategic; Emphasizes long-term structural shifts (GCC, Green Energy) over quarterly noise; Transparent on capex overshoot due to strategic solar bets.
non-obvious takeaways: Solar assets are not just ESG but a commercial moat attracting 'power guzzler' GCCs/data centers; Accelerated depreciation (40%) on solar will artificially boost near-term PAT; Shift from 'landlord arbitrage' to 'service/platform' model with VAS extending beyond owned buildings.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising energy costs and ESG mandates for GCCs | Indiqube Spaces Limited | beneficiary | High | Captive solar provides INR 22-23 Cr savings and attracts high-consumption clients; 100% green power goal is a key differentiator. |
| Need for flexible, premium spoke locations for large MNC hubs | Indiqube Spaces Limited | beneficiary | High | Hub-and-spoke trend drives 20-25% of large portfolios to flex operators; Indiqube's institutional supply pickup aligns with this. |
| Material cost inflation impacting fit-out budgets | Indiqube Spaces Limited | loser | Med | Capex per sq ft rose to INR 1,650 due to 5-7% material inflation, though passed through via rental inflation clauses. |

themes.title: Flexible workspace, PropTech & commercial real-estate services
themes.need: The GCC build-out and hybrid-work shift drive managed/flexible office demand, and Q1FY27 showed flex becoming the marginal buyer of Indian office space. SMARTWORKS grew revenue 44% to INR 546cr with normalized EBITDA INR 107cr (+74%) at a 19.6% margin, lifted GCC clients from 15% to 21% of revenue in a single quarter, and reported India's highest-ever quarterly leasing at 24.6 mn sq ft with 27% of it through flex, up from 19% a year ago. PropTech consolidation started in the same quarter: AURUM announced the acquisition of Housing.com (~24% of India's online-portal share, 58mn monthly visits) at ~1.5x revenue against listed comparables at 4.5-10x, with Housing currently burning ~INR 200cr a year and committed to break even in four to six quarters. AWFIS/EFCIL/INDIQUBE/DEVX/WEWORK add managed workspace; NIRLON on office REIT-proxy assets.
themes.driver: GCC seat-count additions and flex share of net leasing; AURUM's four-to-six-quarter Housing.com breakeven clock; enterprise managed-office wins.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's integrated managed spaces platform combining managed workspaces, interior design & build, workplace operations, digital technology and sustainability solutions across the country's talent-rich micro-markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: IndiQube began as a managed workspace provider and has evolved into an integrated managed spaces platform operating at the intersection of real estate, interiors, operations, technology and sustainability. It delivers plug-and-play managed workspaces (Grow), customised interior design & build/retrofit (DesignQube), managed/facility services for workspaces and retail (IndiQare), green transformation solutions including solar and renovation (Eco), and a connecting digital technology layer (MiQube/ServiQube). Its clients are Global Capability Centres (GCCs), Indian conglomerates, unicorns and high-growth startups across Tier I and Tier II Indian cities.

segment_detail.body: Core Workspace (85% revenue, 18-21% margin); VAS (15% revenue, up from 12%, targeting 17-18%; includes IT products, design-build, transport); Solar (INR 22-23 Cr annual savings, 26.7 MW operational/soon-operational).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Grow:** Plug & Play Managed Workspaces (offices, retail, F&B outlets)
- **DesignQube:** Customised interior design, build and retrofit services
- **IndiQare:** Managed/facility services for workspace and retail operations
- **Eco:** Solar power installations, Green transition / sustainability retrofit solutions
- **MiQube:** MiQube app (tenant platform), ServiQube (service delivery app), AI transport routing, smart space management, geo-spatial attendance, contactless cafeteria ordering, crowd management analytics

guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 25-30%; EBITDA Margin: 18-21%; Order Inflow: 1.5-2.0 Mn sq ft annual addition (33k-44k seats); Capex: ~INR 1,650/sq ft for interiors + INR 125-150 Cr for 30-35 MW solar addition.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Tier-2 city expansion (e.g., Coimbatore) as a 10-year story; Hub-and-Spoke model capturing 20-25% of large MNC portfolios as 'spokes'; Micro-data centers within facilities for power-guzzling GCCs; Renovation of Grade-B to Grade-A assets (25% of portfolio).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's office market delivered record annual absorption of 83.1 million sq. ft. in 2025, led by Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR and Hyderabad, with continued strong GCC leasing (32.8 million sq. ft.)
- India's office sector expected to cross the 1 billion sq. ft. total stock milestone in 2026, with a structural flight-to-quality toward Grade A+ assets and over 65% of upcoming supply in integrated tech parks
- Expansion into emerging Tier-2 markets (e.g. Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Indore, Coimbatore, Kochi, Vadodara) as supply constraints in core business districts push enterprise occupiers to peripheral and non-core locations
- AI-led workplace evolution: share of technology roles requiring AI exposure projected to rise from 20% in 2025 to 31% by 2027, driving demand for high-spec, innovation-led office environments and scalable flexible workspace solutions
- GCCs 2.0 - India's GCC ecosystem strengthening with R&D-focused GCCs expanding 1.3x faster than overall GCC setups since 2020, and Fortune 500 firms scaling integrated campus-style operations (~41% of GCC leasing in 2025)
- Flexible workspace sector maturing into a more disciplined, network-driven ecosystem supported by sustained institutional and public capital inflows
- Structural shift toward 'core + flex' real estate strategies: nearly 55% of occupiers already incorporate flexible workspaces into their portfolios
- GCC-led demand favouring large, standardised, private/managed office formats - 43% of GCCs prefer fully private managed offices per CBRE's 2025 India Office Occupier Survey
- AI-led hiring expected to contribute ~31% of flex seat leasing by CY2030P, emerging as a key driver of future flex demand
- Broadening sectoral and geographic momentum with core sectors entering a high-growth phase (2026-28), supported by AI-led investments, supply chain diversification and infrastructure push

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expanded 300 bps to 21% driven by operating leverage and mature center stabilization (85-90% occupancy); VAS margins lower (10-15%) but accretive to scale/stickiness; Cost headwind: Material inflation added INR 1/sq ft to capex (5-7% bump); Solar savings offset rising grid power costs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on organic growth (1.5-2 Mn sq ft/year); Strategic solar investments for cost arbitrage and client acquisition; No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not discussed in transcript.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 IndiQube added nearly 28,000 seats, 1.25 million sq. ft. of Area Under Management and 15 new centres, taking its portfolio to 130 centres across 17 cities (8 Tier I and 9 Tier II) with 9.66 million sq. ft. under management, guided by its Follow-the-Talent micro-market strategy with Bengaluru as a core anchor market. More than 2.5 million sq. ft. of the portfolio has been created through renovation and transformation of ageing real estate assets. On the renewable-energy side, the company's 20 MW solar farm in Karnataka became fully operational during the year as part of its broader capital programme; this is to be combined with an upcoming 4 MW solar plant in Maharashtra, a 2.7 MW solar farm in Tamil Nadu, and more than 25 rooftop solar installations, aggregating to over 30 MW of solar capacity as the company works toward transitioning its portfolio to 100% green power.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, and strategic; Emphasizes long-term structural shifts (GCC, Green Energy) over quarterly noise; Transparent on capex overshoot due to strategic solar bets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Follow-the-Talent, micro-market-led supply strategy establishing presence where talent, business ecosystems and growth corridors converge
- Asset transformation capability: revitalises ageing commercial real estate (over 50% of India's office stock is estimated to be more than 10 years old); more than 2.5 million sq. ft. of the portfolio created through renovation of ageing assets, unlocking higher margins
- Hub-and-spoke model pairing large hub centres in key micro-markets with smaller spoke centres for reach and accessibility
- Full-stack platform depth (managed spaces, interiors, operations, technology, sustainability) that deepens client relationships and enables cross-sell/upsell as customers expand, strengthening stickiness
- Enterprise orientation with large, sticky client base: 848 clients, 44% of revenue from multi-centre clients, 62% brand-led client acquisition, 56% of revenue from GCC clients, and nearly 90% of occupancy from clients with more than 100 seats
- Digital intelligence layer (MiQube/ServiQube) connecting employees, clients, administrators and service teams — 119K+ app downloads, 1.4 million+ in-app transactions, 36% YoY transaction growth
- Disciplined asset-light operating model aligning occupancy ramp-up and capital recovery: 55-60% occupancy for breakeven, 6 months to breakeven, 85-90% steady-state occupancy, 12 months to steady state, with client lock-in (34 months), fit-out capex recovery (36 months) and landlord lock-in (38 months) synchronised to reduce asset-liability mismatch
- Sustainability embedded across the platform: over 30 MW aggregate solar capacity, nearly 3 million sq. ft. green-certified, multiple green building and management-system certifications

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Quarterly occupancy volatility (ended Q4 at 81% vs 85% prior); Material cost inflation (war impact); Tier-2 supply maturity challenges; Concentration in South India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra); Potential AI impact on low-end hiring (mitigated by premiumization).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Solar assets are not just ESG but a commercial moat attracting 'power guzzler' GCCs/data centers; Accelerated depreciation (40%) on solar will artificially boost near-term PAT; Shift from 'landlord arbitrage' to 'service/platform' model with VAS extending beyond owned buildings.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Follow the Talent strategy: build high-density workspace clusters across talent-rich micro-markets, with South India and Bengaluru continuing as a core anchor market
- Deepen platform capabilities and cross-sell across the client lifecycle through DesignQube (interiors), MiQube (digital layer) and IndiQare (managed services), growing Value-Added Services contribution to revenue
- Maintain a capital-efficient, asset-light operating model by synchronising client lock-in, interior fit-out capex payback and landlord lock-in periods to reduce asset-liability mismatch
- Progress sustainability agenda …

| Rising energy costs and ESG mandates for GCCs | Indiqube Spaces Limited | beneficiary | High | Captive solar provides INR 22-23 Cr savings and attracts high-consumption clients; 100% green power goal is a key differentiator. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Dual reporting] The deck presents IGAAP-equivalent results alongside Ind AS, excluding Ind AS adjustments, as a "supplementary" and "consistent benchmark" for evaluating performance across periods; most operating slides are marked IGAAP Equivalent while cash-EBIT slides are marked Ind AS.
- [Ind AS 116 optics] The company reports an accounting loss under Ind AS while asserting it is PAT positive on an IGAAP-equivalent basis, and points to current income tax expense of 8.4 / 7.67 / 21.73 / 8.14 Rs Cr for FY24 Audited, FY25 Audited, FY26 Audited and Q1 FY27 Estimated as evidence of underlying profitability.
- [Ind AS 116 quantum] Interest on lease liabilities of Rs 116 Cr and depreciation on ROU assets of Rs 148 Cr give a Total Ind AS 116 Impact of Rs 264 Cr, against payment of lease liabilities of Rs (190) Cr, for a stated Net Impact on P&L of Rs 75 Cr (prior-year comparatives 100, 113, 213, (140) and 73).
- [Finance-lease revenue] Under the DesignQube model, design-and-build arrangements are accounted for as financial leases, so income is classified under Other Income under Ind AS; the deck argues it "should be considered part of Revenue from Operations" and adds it back in Adjusted Cash EBIT.
- [Entity] The company is a recently renamed/converted entity — "formerly known as Indiqube Spaces Private Limited, Innovent Spaces Private Limited" — listed on BSE (544454) and NSE (INDIQUBE).
